title: POC to PROD: Hard Lessons from 200+ Enterprise GenAI Deployments - Randall Hunt, Caylent
talk_summary: Randall Hunt of Caylent shares lessons from 200+ enterprise GenAI builds, emphasizing that evals, context management, and economics matter more than model choice.

takeaways.technique: Boolean pass/fail evals instead of scored metrics
takeaways.what_they_do: Start evals from a single vibe-check, then vary inputs to build a small set; use simple true/false success metrics rather than computed scores like BERT.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Metrics do not have to be a score... They can just be a boolean. It can just be true or false. Was this inference successful or not?

takeaways.what_they_do: Put volatile info (dates, per-request context) at the bottom of the prompt after stable instructions so the prefix stays cacheable.
Route offline/batch jobs through batch endpoints, which are discounted across the board.
Determine the smallest context that yields correct inference and strip irrelevant material so the model reasons over less.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Figure out what is the minimum viable context in order to get the correct inference and how can I optimize that context over time.

takeaways.technique: Don't wrap trivial functions as tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Avoid tool calls for things like get_current_date; inject that data directly into the prompt string instead of spending a tool round-trip.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The number of times I see people defining a tool called get current date is infuriating to me... just throw it in the string.

takeaways.technique: Treat model choice as incidental, spec as stable
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep input/output spec and evals fixed while swapping underlying models; they saw drop-in upgrades with no regressions across Claude versions.
